sections.english: My soul, will you ever be good, simple, individual, bare, brighter than the body that covers you? Will you ever taste the disposition to love and affection? Will you ever be complete and free of need, missing nothing, desiring nothing live or lifeless for the enjoyment of pleasure? Or time for longer pleasure, or place, or country, or fine climate, or even human company? Will you not rather be satisfied with your present state, taking pleasure in all your present circumstances?
sections.chinese: 我的魂灵啊，你将会有朝一日变好、变素朴、变为一体、变为赤裸、变得比覆盖你的躯体更为清明吗？你将会有朝一日尝到爱与深情那甘美之性情吗？你将变得完足而一无所缺，错过了无遗、不贪求任何有生或无生之物以享悦逸乐吗？亦不贪求更长之享乐时光，或场所，或异乡，或宜人之气候，或甚至人之相伴吗？你难道不愿满足于当下之状态，在你当下一切之处境中怡然自悦吗？

sections.english: Observe what your physical nature requires, as one subject to the condition of mere life. Then do it and welcome it, as long as your nature as an animate being will not be impaired. Next, you should observe what your nature as an animate being requires: again, adopt all of this, as long as your nature as a rational being will not be impaired. And rationality is also social. Apply these rules and go beyond them no further.
sections.chinese: 观察你之物理本性所需者——作为一仅受生命条件所制约者之所需。然后去做并接纳它，只要那无损于你作为一有生命之存在者的本性。其次，当观察你作为一有生存在者之本性所需者：同样，接纳所有这一切，只要那无损于你作为一理性存在者之本性。而理性亦是社会性之理性。运用这些规则，无可更逾越一步。

sections.english: All that happens is an event either within your natural ability to bear it, or not. So if it is an event within that ability, do not complain, but bear it as you were born to. If outside that ability, do not complain either: it will take you away before you have the chance for complaint. Remember, though, that you are by nature born to bear all that your own judgement can decide bearable, or tolerable, in action.
sections.chinese: 一切所发生之事，其事件要么在你自然承受能力之内，要么不在。若其事在此能力之内，便莫抱怨，只如你生来所当为那般去承受。若其在外于此能力，也莫抱怨：它在你有机会抱怨之前，便会夺你而去。然而切记：你天生自本性上就能承受任何一你自身判断能在行动中判为可堪者、或可为者之事。

sections.english: If he is going wrong, teach him kindly and show him what he has failed to see. If you can't do that, blame yourself — or perhaps not even yourself.
sections.chinese: 若他行差踏错，便以善意点拨他，示知他所未能见及之处。若你做不到，便责怪自己——或也莫要责怪自己。

sections.english: Whatever happens to you was being prepared for you from everlasting, and the mesh of causes was ever spinning from eternity both your own existence and the incidence of this particular happening.
sections.chinese: 凡临到你身之事，自恒远以来早已为你预备好了，那因果之网络自永恒之太初便已同时纺织了你自己之存有与此一特定事件之降临。

sections.english: Whether atoms or a natural order, the first premise must be that I am part of the Whole which is governed by nature. Secondly, I have some close relationship with the other kindred parts. So remembering that I am part of a Whole so constituted will leave me happy with all that happens to me. And in so far as I have some close relationship with the other kindred parts, I shall do nothing unsocial, but rather look to the good of my kin and have every impulse directed to the common benefit and diverted from the opposite.
sections.chinese: 无论是原子或是自然秩序，首要之前提乃是我乃是由自然所统御之宇宙整体之一部分。其次，我与其他同源之部分有着某种亲近之关系。故此，若记取我乃是一如此构成之整体的一部分，便会使我欣然接纳那临到我身之一切。且在同样之层次上，因我与其他同源之部分有着某种亲近之关系，我当不做任何违背社会之事，而当关注同类之利益，并将每一个冲动导引至公共之福祉而远离其反面。

sections.english: Claim your entitlement to these epithets — good, decent, truthful; in mind clear, cooperative, and independent — and take care then not to swap them for other names: and if you do forfeit these titles, return to them quickly. Remember, too, that 'clarity of mind' was meant to signify for you discriminating attention to every detail and the concentration of thought. Launch yourself, then, on these few claims. If you can stay within them, stay there like a man translated to some paradise, the Islands of the Blest. But if you feel yourself falling away and losing control, retire in good heart to some corner where you will regain control — or else make a complete exit from life.
sections.chinese: 你去领受你应得的这些称号——好、端正、真诚；心灵清明、协同而独立——且留心莫要以它们去换别的名分：若你真的失去了这些称号，便迅速返回其中。也当铭记：清明之心智其本意便是标识你于每一细节的那种分辨之专注，以及凝思之聚中。那便向此寥寥数端的资格指标启程奋进吧。若你能栖止于其中，便栖之如一位被接引至某一天堂——至福之群岛——的人。但若你感到自己在滑坠、在失控，则安心退至某一隅，在那里你将重获掌管——否则，便全然退出此生。

sections.english: Farce, war, frenzy, torpor, slavery! Day by day those sacred doctrines of yours will be wiped out, whenever you conceive and admit them untested by natural philosophy. Every perception, every action must both satisfy the circumstantial and exercise the theoretical, so that you preserve the confidence of right knowledge in every particular, yet keep it unobtrusive.
sections.chinese: 闹剧、战争、疯狂、僵麻、奴役！你那诸般神圣之教义日复一日渐被抹去——每当你在未经自然哲学之验证的情形下就构想它们、采纳它们时，便是如此。每一知觉、每一行动都须既满足具体情境之需要，同时也履行并锻炼那理论法则，如此，你方能于每一具体物事中保守正确知见之确信，却又决不使之锋芒外露。

sections.english: A spider is proud to trap a fly. Men are proud of their own hunting — a hare, a sprat in the net, boars, bears, Sarmatian prisoners. If you examine their motives, are they not all bandits?
sections.chinese: 蜘蛛以捕捉苍蝇而骄傲。人则为自己的猎获而得意——一只兔、网中之幼鱼、野猪、熊、萨尔马提亚战俘。若你检审其动机，他们岂不是皆为强盗吗？

sections.english: Adopt a systematic study of the way all things change into one another: pay constant attention to this aspect of nature and train yourself in it. Nothing is so conducive to greatness of mind.
sections.chinese: 系统性地研习万物彼此互变之道：恒切关注自然这一侧面，并在其中训练自己。无一物能如此助益于心灵之壮阔。

sections.english: What need of prompt or hint when it is open to yourself to discern what needs to be done — and, if you can see your way, to follow it with kind but undeviating intent. If you cannot see the way, hold back and consult your best advisers. If some other factors obstruct this advice, proceed on your present resources with careful deliberation, holding to what is clearly just.
sections.chinese: 若你自己便能辨识何者需为——且若你能看清道路，便怀着善意而不移不易之志去追随它——那还用得着什么提示暗示呢？若你看不清路，便暂且停住，请教你最好的谋士们。若另有些因素阻碍了这些建议之执行，则倚靠你当下可用之资，沉谋稳重地推进，持守明确之正义。

sections.english: As soon as you wake from sleep ask yourself: 'Will it make any difference to you if others criticize what is in fact just and true?' No, it will not. You have surely not forgotten what these people who whinny in praise or blame of others are like in their bed and at their board, the sort of things they do or shun, how they steal or grab, not with hands and feet but with the most precious part of themselves, which gives birth, as the choice goes, to trust, decency, truth, law, a good divinity within.
sections.chinese: 一朝醒来，便问自己：「若别人批评那事实上是正确而真实之物，这对你能有何不同呢？」不，决然不能。你必然不曾忘记这些在夸骂别人时嘶嘶叫叫的人，在床席上、餐几边是何种模样，他们所为与所回避的那一类事，他们以何等方式窃取掠夺——不用手足，而用他们自身最珍贵之部分：此一部分，随其自择，能给诞信心、端正、真理、法律，及一内在之善好神明。

sections.english: Nature gives all and takes all back. To her the man educated into humility says: 'Give what you will; take back what you will.' And he says this in no spirit of defiance, but simply as her loyal subject.
sections.chinese: 自然给予一切，也收取一切。于她面前，那受教而养出谦逊之心的人说道：「凡你所愿赐者，请赐；凡你所愿收回者，便收回。」他这样说着，全无任何抗拒之心情，仅作为她忠实顺从之子民而言之。

sections.english: The time you have left is short. Live it as if you were on a mountain. Here or there makes no difference, if wherever you live you take the world as your city. Let men see, let them observe a true man living in accordance with nature. If they cannot bear him, let them kill him — a better fate than a life like theirs.
sections.chinese: 你余剩之时间不多了。将它当做你在山巅上那般而活。这里或那里并无区别，只要不论在何处你都将世界视作你的城邦。让人们看见，让他们观察一个依照自然而生活的真实之人。若他们无法容忍他，便让他们杀了他吧——这总好过像他们那般苟活于世。

sections.english: No more roundabout discussion of what makes a good man. Be one!
sections.chinese: 再莫绕圈子讨论什么成就一良善之人。自己去做一个便是！

sections.english: Keep constantly in your mind an impression of the whole of time and the whole of existence — and the thought that each individual thing is, on the scale of existence, a mere fig-seed; on the scale of time, one turn of a drill.
sections.chinese: 在你心中恒常保持对整个时间与整个存有之印象——且常抱持此念：每一单独之事物，在存有之尺度上，不过一粒无花果之籽种；在时间之尺度上，不过是一次钻针之旋转。

sections.english: Consider any existing object and reflect that it is even now in the process of dissolution and change, in a sense regenerating through decay or dispersal: in other words, to what sort of 'death' each thing is born.
sections.chinese: 思及任何现存之对象，作如此之反思：它即便此刻已在消解与变化的过程中了，在某种意义上，它正透过腐烂或消散在不断更新——换言之，每一样物事皆是为某一种「死亡」而生的。

sections.english: What sort of people are they when eating, sleeping, coupling, shitting, etc.? Then what are they like when given power over men? Haughty, quick to anger, punishing to excess. And yet just now they were slaves to all those needs for all those reasons: and shortly they will be slaves again.
sections.chinese: 当他们进食、睡觉、交媾、排泄等等之时，是何种样人？而后，当他们既得控人之权柄时，又变成了何般模样？傲慢不逊、易怒、罚越其度。然而就在刚才，他们还为诸般需求之种种理由而当着奴隶：且不久他们又将复为奴隶。

sections.english: What universal nature brings to each is brought to his benefit. The benefit stands at the time of its bringing.
sections.chinese: 宇宙自然带给每个人之物，皆是为其利益而带来。这利益，就立于其被带至的时刻。

sections.english: 'Earth loves the rain, the proud sky loves to give it.' The whole world loves to create futurity. I say then to the world, 'I share your love.' Is this not the source of the phrase, 'This loves to happen'?
sections.chinese: 「大地恋雨」，骄傲之穹苍「乐于赐雨」。整个世界皆爱创造将来。那么，我对这世界说，「我与你怀有同一之爱。」这不正是那句「此事乐耶发生耳」之语源么？

sections.english: Either you live on here, used to it now; or you retire, your own decision to leave; or you die, your service done. No other choice. Be cheerful, then.
sections.chinese: 要么你继续活在此地，至今也已惯了；要么你自行退去，依己之决定而离去；要么你死去，你之服役已经完成。别无可选。那么，常持乐悦之态吧。

sections.english: Always have clear in your mind that 'the grass is not greener' elsewhere, and how everything is the same here as on the top of a mountain, or on the sea-shore, or wherever you will.
sections.chinese: 恒常清楚记在你之心中：别处之草并不更绿，一切在此处且与在山巅上、或在海岸边、或在任何你所愿之所在，皆一般相同。

sections.english: What is my directing mind to me? What am I turning it into now, what use am I making of it? Is it drained of intelligence? Is it divorced and broken off from society? Is it so interfused and welded to the flesh that it sways with its tides?
sections.chinese: 我之主导心灵于我而言究为何物？我此刻正将其转变作什么，我又是把它当作何等用途而加以运用？它是否被抽干枯尽至于空无智性？它是否已被剥离割裂而脱离了社会？它是否已如此交融而与骨肉焊接在一处，致使其随其躯体之潮汐而起伏摇摆？

sections.english: A slave running from his master is a fugitive. Law is our master: the law-breaker is therefore a fugitive. But also in the same way pain, anger, or fear denote refusal of some past, present, or future order from the governor of all things — and this is law, which legislates his lot for each of us. So the man who is subject to pain, anger, or fear is a fugitive.
sections.chinese: 自其主人而逃的奴隶是一逃犯。法律是我等之主人：故此违法者便是逃犯。然疼痛、愤怒或恐惧等，亦以同样之方式表示对其一过去、现在或将来自那统御万有者之次序的拒斥——而此即是他为吾辈每一人配定命运之法也。所以，那受制于痛苦、愤怒或恐惧的人，便是逃犯。

sections.english: A man deposits his sperm in a womb and goes away. Thereafter another cause takes over, does its work, and produces a baby. What a result from what a beginning! Then again. The child takes food down its throat, and now another causal sequence takes over, creating sensation and impulse, the whole of life and strength, and all the other results: what a product!
sections.chinese: 一个人将精子注入一子宫，径自离去。其后另一原因接手，尽其工作，产出一婴孩。这是由何种之始产生了何种之果！再之，孩子摄进食物经由其喉，此时另一因缘序列又接手介入，创生了感觉、冲动，以及整体之生命与力量，并所有其余之果实：这是何等之产物！

sections.english: Constantly reflect that all the things which happen now have happened before: reflect too that they will happen again in the future. Have in your mind's eye whole dramas with similar settings, all that you know of from your own experience or earlier history.
sections.chinese: 恒常反思：如今所发生之一切事，全都在从前发生过：也要反思：它们将来亦会复现。在你心目中，历历映现完整之诸出剧幕，场景何其相似——所有你自自身经验抑或较早历史中所知之一切情景。

sections.english: Picture everyone voicing pain or discontent at anything, as like a pig at a sacrifice, kicking and squealing. Just the same is the man who keeps it to himself, silently resentful on his bed. Think of all the threads that bind us, and how only rational creatures are given the choice of submitting willingly to providence: mere submission is necessity for all.
sections.chinese: 试想一下，凡为某事发出痛楚或不满之声的人，都类如一只祭祀中之猪，尥蹄而嘶嚎。同样，那掩于一己之内自己之床位上默然怀怨的人，也并无不同。想想这些将我等系在一起的繁多丝线，并想想唯理性之造物才被赋予了那心甘情愿顺服于天意之选项：而所有愚蠢的造物，其顺服仅是必然。

sections.english: Consider each individual thing you do and ask yourself whether to lose it through death makes death itself any cause for fear.
sections.chinese: 思及你所做之每一单独之事，并扪心自问：若因死亡而失去此物，此事是否使死亡本身构成了堪畏的理由？

sections.english: Whenever you take offence at the wrong done by another, move on at once to consider what similar wrong you are committing — it could be setting value on money, or pleasure, or reputation, and so on through the categories. This reflection will quickly damp your anger, aided by the further thought that he is acting under compulsion: what else could he do? Or, if you can, remove the compulsion.
sections.chinese: 每当你对他人所犯之过错感到冒犯，当即转而省思你自己究竟所犯同类之过错是何——或是把价值寄托在金钱上，或是逸乐上，或是名声上，或通此等类别中的任何一者。此番省思将迅速消解你之愤怒，而如果再辅以另一重思量的话——即他乃是受迫而行事：试问他还能怎样？——则效果更佳。或，若你能除去那种强迫，便图而为之。

sections.english: When you see Satyrion or Eutyches or Hymen, picture them in Socrates' circle; when you see Eutychion or Silvanus, picture Euphrates; when you see Tropaeophorus, picture Alciphron; when you see Severus, picture Crito or Xenophon; and when you look at yourself, picture one of the Caesars — for each, then picture the counterpart. Then let this thought strike you: 'Where are they now?' Nowhere — or who knows where?
sections.chinese: 你看见萨堤里翁或欧提刻斯或许门时，便想象他们在苏格拉底那个圈中；看见欧提基翁或西尔瓦努斯时，便想象欧弗拉特斯；看见特洛派奥弗鲁斯时，便想象阿尔基弗朗；看见塞维鲁斯时，便想象克力同或色诺芬；而当你审视自己时，则想着某位凯撒——换句话说，替每一人，想出其匹配之对应者。接着，让此念触动你：「他们如今安在？」无处可觅——又或者，又有谁知其在何处？

sections.english: Let no one have the chance to accuse you, with any truth, of not being sincere or a good man: make sure that anyone taking this view of you is a liar. This is wholly up to you — who is there to prevent you being good and sincere? You must just decide to live no longer if you won't have these qualities. Not even does reason dictate living in the absence of reason.
sections.chinese: 莫给任何人以一丝一毫之真正凭据来指责你不真诚或不是个好人：确保任何这般看你的人，都是一个说谎者。此事全然在你——谁又能拦阻你做一个好人、做真诚的人呢？你只须下定决心：若你不能具备这些品质，便不再生存下去。即便是理性，也不要求你在一无理性之状态中存续。

sections.english: Now the roller does not have the gift of following its own movement wherever it will, nor does water or fire, or anything else subject to a nature or life without reason: there are many barriers or impediments in their way. But mind and reason have the power, by their nature and at their will, to move through every obstacle. Keeping clear in your view this easy facility of reason to carry through all things — like fire rising, a stone falling, a roller on a slope — stop looking for anything more. Any remaining hindrances either come from the corpse which is our body, or — without the judgement and consent of our own reason — cause no damage and do no evil: otherwise anyone meeting such hindrance would immediately become bad himself.
sections.chinese: 滚轮并无追随它自身滚动、想去哪里就去哪里的天赋，水与火亦然，任何受制于某一无理性之自然或生命之一切其他物事亦然：它们之路途上有许多栅栏阻碍。但心灵与理性却有此一力量，依其本性与其意志，逾越一切障碍而前进。在你眼前清清晰晰地观看理性这份轻松穿透一切万物的能力吧——如火焰上腾，如石块下落，如滚轮沿斜坡而下——然后便不要再顾盼任何其余之物。所留之一切剩余障碍，要么出于吾辈之尸身即吾辈之躯体，要么——在没有己身理性之判断与同意之下——既不会造成伤害，也不构成恶事；否则，任何人一旦遭遇这类阻碍，便立时会变成坏人了。

sections.english: One bitten by the true doctrines needs only a very short and commonplace reminder to lose all pain and fear — for instance: 'Your children are no more than leaves. Leaves too these loud voices of loyal praise, these curses from your opponents, this silent blame or mockery: mere leaves likewise the letters from posterity which will pass on your fame. All these things come round again in spring; then the wind drops them, and the forest grows more to take their place. Short-lived is all there is, yet you pursue or shun as if it were eternal.'
sections.chinese: 一被真道所咬之人，只需极区区且通俗之一点省醒，便足以丢掉一切苦楚与恐惧——比如：「你的子女亦不过尔尔树叶而已。这般那些高声歌功之忠敬赞颂、这般那些来自于你敌手之咒骂，这般那些默然之责斥或嘲讽——无不属于树叶；那将从后人中寄来传递你名声的种种书函，也都同样是些叶子罢了。所有这些皆在春天复又轮至；然后风将它们扫落，林木又长出更多的来替代。所存有之一切皆是昙花一现，然而你却竟似其永恒那般追逐或回避。」

sections.english: The healthy eye must look at all there is to be seen, and not say 'I only want pale colours' — this is a symptom of disease. The healthy ear and nose must be ready for all sounds or smells, and the healthy stomach must accept all food in the same way that a mill accepts all it was made to grind. So too the healthy mind must be ready for all that happens. A mind which says 'My children must live' or 'All men must praise all I do' is like an eye demanding pale colours or teeth soft food.
sections.chinese: 健全之眼应看那一切可看之物，而不是说「我只要灰淡之色」——此乃疾病之症候。健全之耳与鼻应能纳受一切声音或气味，健全之胃亦须纳受一切食物，如同磨坊纳受一切它被造以为之碾磨的谷物一样。同样，健全之心灵也须为所发生之一切备便就绪。一心灵若说：「我的孩子必须活下去」或「所有人都须来赞美我所行之一切」，便仿似一只眼睛只要看灰淡之色，或一副牙齿只吃柔软之食。

sections.english: No one is so fortunate as not to have standing round his deathbed some people who welcome the fate coming on him. Was he the earnest sage? Then maybe there will be someone at his final moment saying to himself: 'We can breathe again now, rid of this schoolmaster. He was not hard on any one of us, but I could feel his silent criticism of us all.' So much for the earnest sage. As for the rest of us, consider how many other reasons there are for a host of people to want rid of us. You will think of this when dying: 'I am leaving a life in which even my closest companions, for whom I strove, prayed, worried so much, themselves wish me to go.' Why would anyone grasp at a longer stay in the world?
sections.chinese: 没人能如此幸运，使其临终之床旁连一个欢迎那降临到他身上之命运的人也没有。他是那严肃的智者么？那么也许在他最后一刻，会有人心内自念道：「我们总算又能透过气来了，终于除掉了这个蹩师。他从没格外苛待我们哪一个过，但我能感觉到他那沉默的、对我们所有人的批评。」严肃之智者，风光如此。至若我们其余之人，且想有多少别的原因，会使得一大帮人想除掉我们。你临终之际将思及此节：「我将离开的这生涯中，即便是那些我最亲密的同伴——那些我为之奋斗、为之祈祷、为之焦心得要命的伙伴——他们竟然都希望我离开。」那又为何还恋世多挨一刻呢？

sections.english: As far as you can, get into the habit of asking yourself in relation to any action taken by another: 'What is his point of reference here?' But begin with yourself: examine yourself first.
sections.chinese: 只要你能够，养成如此之习惯：于别人所做之任何行动，反首问一己：「他此举之参照据准是什么？」但请先从你自己开始：先检审你自己。

sections.english: Remember that what pulls the strings is that part of us hidden inside: that is the power to act, that is the principle of life, that, one could say, is the man himself. So never give any equal thought to the vessel which contains it or the organs built round it. These are an instrument like an axe, differing only in that they are grown onto the body.
sections.chinese: 切记：那拉动绳线者乃是我们内中那隐而不见的部分：那即是行事之能力，那即是生命之原则，那——可谓——就是此一人自身。故此，永勿以同等之思虑去考量容载其的那一器皿，亦莫关注那构筑在它周围之诸般器官。这些器官不过是一件如斧头般的工具而已，它之差异，仅在于它们是长在了躯体之上罢了。
